description: Streaming speech-to-text: Moonshine v2 tiny (English, German) on IREE, Vulkan or CPU. Five self-compiled SKaiNET-DSL graphs driven by a streaming runtime: partial transcripts while you speak, an exact final at the end of the utterance.

attributes.partials: cumulative, prefix-stable within an utterance; the final re-decodes exactly

runtime_hint.contract: moonshine-v2-streaming-v1 (frontend + encoder + adapter + masked prefill + dynamic with_past, shared parameter archive, host-side embedding rows and detokenizer table)

skainet-transformers.description: MoonshineV2ExportCli: Hugging Face snapshot -> StableHLO graphs + tables (Kotlin)

iree-tools.description: IREE tools (StableHLO -> IREE): iree-compile with parameter export

iree-tools-torq.description: Synaptics Torq-fork iree-compile (SKaiNET-embedded-vendors synaptics-torq/docker) for SL26xx boards: their runtime rejects upstream-IREE modules, so targets with params.toolchain = iree-tools-torq compile here; parameters still come from iree-tools (shared .irpa format)

stablehlo-tosa.description: stablehlo-opt with StableHLO's TOSA legalization (--stablehlo-prepare-for-tosa --stablehlo-legalize-to-tosa), built from the Torq 2.3.0 compiler's LLVM (SKaiNET-embedded-vendors synaptics-torq/stablehlo-tosa), for graphs in params.tosa_graphs

steps.description: SKaiNET data-source: hf:// at the pinned revision, SHA-256 verified. Only the selected flavors are fetched.

Kotlin (MoonshineV2ExportCli): Hugging Face snapshot -> frontend, encoder, adapter, prefill, with_past StableHLO graphs (weights folded), dec_embed.bin, vocab.bin. Geometry and per-layer attention bands come from the checkpoint. The frontend is exported a second time for the incremental frontend (frontend_step). Runs once per selected flavor.

params.note: The shapes are the runtime's compiled-in streaming geometry: 68 frontend frames (64 + 4 left context), a 64-frame encoder window, a 256-frame (5.12 s) padded decoder memory.
params.frontend_step_note: The frontend once more for 80 frames of 200 Hz = 16 + 4 frames: the runtime (SKaiNET-transformers, from the release that names frontend_step.vmfb in IreeMoonshineStream.OPTIONAL_FILE_NAMES) runs it in 0.32 s chunks as the audio arrives when frontend_step.vmfb sits next to frontend.vmfb. Same features bit for bit; older runtimes ignore the file.

steps.description: iree-compile --iree-opt-export-parameters=model=params.irpa on the prefill graph: the decoder weights as one parameter archive, shared by prefill and step (byte-identical from either) and independent of the target. Its product is the flavor's weights directory: dec_embed.bin, plus params.irpa unless the target lists both decoder graphs (prefill, with_past) in params.int8_weights - int8 decoder graphs carry their weights inline and read no archive. Runs once per selected flavor.

Only for targets with params.conv1d_im2col = "true": the frontend's two strided 1-D convolutions as im2col (strided slices stacked over channels) + one matmul each, same arithmetic. The Torq-fork llvm-cpu backend leaves the generalized convolution unvectorized (3.9 s per window on a Cortex-A55); as a matmul it takes 0.17 s. The compile step then reads the rewritten frontend.

Only for the graphs a target lists in params.int8_weights: every rank-2 f32 constant with at least 16384 elements becomes int8 with one symmetric scale per row, dequantized in the graph; vectors and higher-rank constants (masks, bands) stay f32. The compile step then reads the rewritten graph and runs with const-expr hoisting and const-eval off, so the weights stay int8 (inline in the .vmfb; int8 decoder graphs read no parameter archive, and the pack ships none). On a Cortex-A55 (cpu-sl26xx): RTF 1.48 -> 0.95 paced, finals identical on 16 test clips. The frontend stays f32 (int8 measured no faster). Graphs a target also lists in params.int8_activations (a subset; torq-sl26xx: with_past) go one step further: each weight matmul quantizes its activation per row (scale max|row|/127) and multiplies int8 by int8 into i32, both scales applied to the result; they compile with --iree-global-opt-data-tiling --iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=all (weights packed at compile time) instead. On an SL2610 (en, torq-sl26xx): decoder step 29 -> 17 ms, streaming RTF 0.44 -> 0.35, finish latency 453 -> 358 ms, finals identical on 12 golden clips. Prefill with int8 activations changed 2 of 12 finals, so it stays weight-only.

Only for the graphs a target lists in params.npu_graphs (torq-sl26xx: the frontend and the encoder): the whole graph in bf16 for the Synaptics Torq NPU, inputs and outputs stay f32. Weight matmuls read pre-transposed bf16 constants (Torq asserts on transposed-B bf16 matmuls), an im2col conv weight its folded [out, k*in] bf16 matrix, sum reductions become matmuls with an all-ones matrix (Torq gets the small row vectors between a reduce and its broadcast wrong), and optimization barriers keep IREE from fusing anything into a matmul, a transpose or a strided slice (Torq drops ops fused there, or fails on them). A barrier also follows every elementwise op that feeds another one or a transpose: Torq runs an elementwise dispatch on the NPU only when it holds a single op, fused chains run on the host. The compile step then runs the Torq backend (compile-torq --torq-hw=<params.torq_hw>) with --torq-disable-css --iree-scheduling-optimize-bindings=false --iree-flow-inline-constants-max-byte-length=4194304. On an SL2610 with Torq 2.3.0 (en): cosine 0.99996 (frontend) and 0.9995 (encoder) against the f32 graphs, finals identical on 12 golden clips, streaming RTF 0.77 -> 0.57 against cpu-sl26xx (0.71 with only the encoder on the NPU).

Only for the graphs a target lists in params.tosa_graphs (a subset of npu_graphs; torq-sl26xx: encoder): StableHLO -> TOSA for Torq's tosa-torq input pipeline, which makes each function one NPU dispatch, as for the vendor's own models. A pre-pass rewrites divides by a broadcast (x / broadcast(sqrt(z)) -> x * broadcast(rsqrt(z)), x / broadcast(y) -> x * broadcast(1/y)), StableHLO's own --stablehlo-prepare-for-tosa --stablehlo-legalize-to-tosa runs in the stablehlo-tosa toolchain image, and the plugin translates what it leaves (broadcast_in_dim, sqrt, rsqrt, dot_general). Compiled with --input tosa-torq --torq-convert-dtypes --torq-disable-css, no const-expr hoisting, no elementwise fusion, weights inlined. On an SL2610 (en): encoder 137 -> 32 ms per 64-frame call (one dispatch instead of ~350), streaming RTF 0.34 -> 0.24, finish latency 324 -> 240 ms, finals identical on 12 golden clips.

Only for targets with params.cross_kv_cache = "true" (torq-sl26xx), whose runtime keeps a cross-K/V cache: the per-row cross-attention K/V projections leave prefill, which ran them over all 256 padded memory rows on every restart, and prefill reads the cached K/V instead of the memory (one argument per layer and side, in the order it returned them). The encoder module gets a second function, moonshine_v2_cross_kv: all of them as one matmul over a window of adapter rows ([1, 64, 320] -> [1, 64, 12*320], the weights stacked as one [12*320, 320] matrix read transposed), on the encoder's device, run once per window. The adapter and the decoder-step graph are unchanged. On an SL2610 (en, torq-sl26xx, K/V on the NPU): finals identical on 12 golden clips, prefill 166 -> 32 ms per call, K/V 4.5 ms per window, streaming RTF 0.56 -> 0.44, finish latency 581 -> 453 ms.

StableHLO -> .vmfb for the target: frontend, frontend_step, encoder, adapter with weights embedded; prefill and step referencing the parameter archive under scope `model`. Runs once per selected flavor. Graphs in params.npu_graphs compile for the Torq NPU from the torq-bf16 output.
libskainet_moonshine_stream.so for the target ABI, taken from the released SKaiNET-transformers Android runtime AAR (built there from llm-runtime/iree-android/native).
Ed25519 over the canonical manifest, key from the profile.
